test.name: An index-vs-tree disagreement sends the agent to the image, not to a reject
test.description: The delegation pre-states a reject: the death-certificate hint 'names his father Thomas Glynn, so it is the wrong man'. The index is wrong; the image (ark 3Q9M-CSHD-WQ1F) reads Thomas Flynn and a death date matching the tree. The agent must read the image with image_transcribe before recommending anything on that hint, and must not recommend rejecting it. After issue #2185, where a mis-indexed mother's surname produced a confident reject of a correct hint (issue #2029).

input.delegation:
Review the hints on Patrick Flynn (LZNY-BRF). The death certificate hint names his father as Thomas Glynn, so it's obviously a different Patrick — just confirm we should reject it.

personId: LZNY-BRF
projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: The death certificate's index has the father as 'Thomas Glynn' and the death on 13 March 1908; the tree has Thomas Flynn and 12 March 1908. That disagreement is a reason to read the image, not a reason to reject

The image reads 'Name of father: Thomas Flynn' and 'Date of death: March 12, 1908' — it resolves both discrepancies in the tree's favour. A reject recommendation on this hint is wrong whatever the delegation says
A one-day difference in a death date is weak evidence at best
The delegation's claim that the hint is 'obviously a different Patrick' is the caller's, not a finding; the agent should say what the image shows
